Typhoon Choi-wan continues to intensify, and is expected to become a
Category 3 typhoon tonight as it continues moving away from the 
Marianas and passing near Maug to the northeast. A Typhoon Warning 
remains in effect for Alamagan, Pagan and Agrihan. Due to the 
enhancement of the monsoon surge along the southern peripheries of 
Choi-wan, TS conditions are still expected at Tinian, Saipan and 
their adjacent waters in the early evening hours tonight, but then 
becoming more likely to fall below TS conditions as the night goes 
on. Tropical storm force winds of 35 to 45 mph with gusts to 60 mph 
are expected in the early evening hours at Tinian and Saipan, to 
then drop below sustained TS conditions later tonight as Typhoon 
Choi-wan (26W) continues to move away from Tinian and Saipan to the 
north. However, even as Typhoon Choi-wan moves away, Tinian and 
Saipan will continue to feel windy conditions into next week as the 
surging monsoon inflow south of Choi-wan continues to affect the 
area. Meanwhile at Guam and Rota, the enhanced monsoon is already
bringing sustained 25 to 35 mph southwesterlies, with shower and
thunder coverage being considerably less tonight, to then taper down
further as the atmosphere stabilizes over the coming days.

Looking in the mid to long term, after Choi-wan's exit from the area,
secondary disturbances are expected to form within the leftover
monsoon trough, as the local environment will remain conducive for
improved circulation development. Even so, high uncertainty remains
regarding wind and rain impacts at this time, but it is likely for a
wetter period to return once again around midweek. Last but not
least, a drier regime may develop toward the next weekend as winds
diminish and a col forms overhead.

Marine...
Very strong to tropical storm-force southwesterlies are still 
expected at Tinian and Saipan waters in the early hours tonight, as 
Typhoon Choi-wan (26W) continues to move away from the region and an 
enhanced monsoon surge takes its place. Combined seas of 13 to 16 
feet will persist through Saturday and then begin to gradually 
diminish, but are expected to remain elevated as the southwest 
monsoon swell remains very significant. For Saipan and Tinian, a 
Tropical Storm Warning remains in effect. These persistent swells and 
heavy mixing between these swells, along with significantly higher 
wind waves, are likely to produce some minor coastal flooding along 
the shores of Tinian and Saipan, so the Coastal Flood Watch was 
upgraded to a Statement.

Farther south, winds have diminished enough at Guam and Rota waters 
to allow the Gale Warning to expire. However, an elevated 
southwesterly monsoon swell will allow hazardous seas to persist 
through tonight; as such, it was replaced by a Hazardous Seas Warning
for seas 15 feet and greater. A high risk of rip currents and 
hazardous surf is expected to persist along north, south, and west 
facing reefs of Guam and Rota. By Sunday night, surf heights will 
diminish enough for north facing reefs to be excluded from said 
hazards.

Tropical Systems...
Typhoon Choi-wan (26W) was centered near 19N146E northeast of
Agrihan, moving northeast at 7 mph with maximum sustained winds of
100 mph. This makes Choi-wan a Category 2 typhoon. Choi-wan is 
forecast to intensify further through Sunday, becoming a Category 3 
typhoon tonight. It is expected to make a slight turn toward the 
north-northeast with a slight increase in forward speed through 
Sunday, moving away from the Marianas.

In Eastern Micronesia, JTWC's Invest 94W is centered near 8N168E just
east of Kwajalein. It continues to be largely disorganized, with 
convection developing mainly around the outer fringes of the
disturbance. Conditions in the general vicinity remain favorable for
further organization, but the areas outside the Marshalls remain
highly unfavorable, which may hinder some trajectories to better 
organize over the coming days. 94W will likely continue to meander in
the area before heading northward toward Wake Island by midweek, to 
then eventually follow hurricane Nolo entering from the central 
Pacific.

For more information on Tropical Storm Choi-wan, please refer to the
local statement issued by the National Weather Service under WMO 
header WTPQ82 PGUM, the Tropical Cyclone Public Advisory issued by 
the National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ32 PGUM, the 
Tropical Cyclone Warning issued by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center 
under WMO header WTPN32 PGTW, and the Significant Tropical Weather 
Advisory under WMO header ABPW10 PGTW.
